subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Dizygotic and Monozygotic Twins and Chorionicity

steps.tx: Twins from two separately fertilised eggs are **dizygotic twins**. They are genetically ordinary siblings and always have two placentas, fused or separate. Rising maternal age and assisted conception increase their frequency. Dizygotic twinning runs in families through raised follicle stimulating hormone and is commoner in West African populations.
steps.say: Dizygotic twins come from two eggs and always have two placentas.

steps.tx: Twins from one fertilised egg splitting form **monozygotic twins**. Timing of the split decides chorionicity and amnionicity. Late splits share a placenta and its vascular dangers. Split before day three gives two placentas; days four to eight one placenta and two sacs; later splits share the sac.
steps.say: Monozygotic twins split from one egg, and split timing decides their membranes.

nodes.label: Split in first days, two placentas

steps.tx: Whether twins share a placenta, determining surveillance intensity, is **chorionicity**. It is assigned accurately only in the first trimester. Monochorionic twins need fortnightly scans from sixteen weeks for transfusion syndrome. The lambda sign is best seen at 11 to 14 weeks and becomes unreliable as pregnancy advances.
steps.say: Chorionicity is assigned in the first trimester and monochorionic twins need fortnightly scans.

steps.tx: A thick membrane insertion with a triangular placental extension is the **lambda sign**. Also called the twin peak sign, it indicates dichorionic twins. Its presence is most reliable before fourteen weeks. Between the membranes at the T, no placental tissue extends, which is the point the examiner must describe.
steps.say: The lambda or twin peak sign indicates dichorionic twins before fourteen weeks.

steps.tx: A thin membrane meeting the placenta at a right angle without extension is the **T sign**. It marks monochorionic diamniotic twins. These twins share placental vessels beneath their separate sacs. They make up about eight percent of monozygotic twins and under one percent of all twin pregnancies.
steps.say: The T sign marks monochorionic diamniotic twins sharing placental vessels.

steps.tx: Twins sharing both placenta and amniotic sac are **monochorionic monoamniotic** and rarest. Cord entanglement threatens both twins throughout pregnancy. Planned caesarean at thirty two to thirty four weeks is usual. Internal podalic version is never attempted in monoamniotic pairs because entangled cords tighten unpredictably.
steps.say: Monochorionic monoamniotic twins risk cord entanglement and deliver by planned caesarean early.

steps.tx: Dichorionic twins are watched monthly while monochorionic need fortnightly review, a **surveillance schedule difference**. Growth discordance and fluid imbalance are the targets in monochorionic pairs. Delivery timing also differs by chorionicity. An 18 to 25 percent weight difference earns closer surveillance even before the formal discordance threshold.
steps.say: Surveillance schedules differ, with monochorionic twins scanned fortnightly from sixteen weeks.

steps.tx: Labelling twins consistently as presenting and non presenting across scans prevents errors, termed **twin labelling**. Discordance calculations depend on comparing the same fetus serially. A labelling map in the notes records sac position and sex. Twin A stays the presenting twin by definition at each scan, and any relabelling is documented with a diagram.
steps.say: Consistent twin labelling prevents errors in serial growth comparison.

steps.tx: Uncomplicated dichorionic twins deliver around thirty seven weeks and monochorionic around thirty six, following **chorionicity delivery timing**. Monoamniotic pairs deliver earliest by caesarean. These timings balance stillbirth against prematurity. Stillbirth risk rises after these gestations, which is the evidence base behind the planned timings.
steps.say: Delivery timing follows chorionicity, balancing stillbirth against prematurity.
